name: Xilinx Alveo U250/U280 (used FPGA accelerator card)
memory_bandwidth_basis: Alveo U280: 64GB DDR4 across 4 DIMM channels, ~77 GB/s aggregate (plus 8GB HBM2 on U280 at ~460 GB/s but not usable as a single pool). U250: 64GB DDR4 similar. These are datacenter-FPGA specs, not a turnkey LLM path.
notes: Added in the Phase-A gap-fill for the Oct-14 research ingest. Used Alveo U250/U280 cards flood eBay at ~$200-2000, and research-exotic.md flags them as a confirmed PAPERWEIGHT for LLM inference: there is no maintained, load-a-GGUF-and-go FPGA LLM stack. Academic flows (SEDA-LLM, custom HLS designs) exist but require you to *become the compiler* - bitstream work, memory-controller tuning, quantization by hand. That is a research project, not inference. Cheap used Alveo = paperweight unless the goal is FPGA development itself.
